These populations are not interchangeable. Actual rosters remain service-specific; definitions do not create a recipient duty where this selected rule has none.

Compared responsibly and likely: disclosure uses good judgment and avoids broadcasting adversary-helpful details, without excusing required recipient reporting; likely is contextual reasonable probability, not certainty or a fixed percentage. These are interpretive context only where the selected rule invokes them; actual judgments require facts.

Compared all five bound impact/effect definitions. Potential agency impact is cumulative across agency customers. Minimal means noticeable to some users; narrow includes some-user interruption under 12 hours OR extremely limited federal-data compromise; disruptive includes many-user interruption under 24 hours OR large/many-type compromise; debilitating includes most-user interruption OR most federal-data compromise, with unknown effect treated as debilitating until proven otherwise. These effect-duration boundaries classify impact, not report deadlines. They do not impose PAIN reporting on unrelated certification or assessment rules. Actual effect and agency count remain factual uncertainties.
